problems.stem: Your slide uses a chart you found online and a paragraph drafted by AI. Which attribution shows you handled credit correctly?
options: No source line, because the chart was free to view.
A caption: 'Chart: U.S. BLS, 2025 (public domain)' and a note 'Summary drafted with AI, edited by me' where disclosure is required.
A line saying 'image from the internet.'
Nothing, since you reworded the AI text slightly.
problems.explanation: Correct attribution names the real source and license for the media and discloses AI assistance where required.

problems.stem: Which note gives BigAL a concrete attribution problem to check?
options: Slide 4 cites a 2025 report URL, but the page does not contain the 18% figure I quoted. Did I cite the wrong source?
problems.explanation: The note names a specific mismatch between the claim and the linked source, so feedback can verify it.

problems.stem: What is a defensible way to use AI when handling citations?
options: Ask AI to generate citations and trust them without checking the sources exist.
Ask AI to format a reference you supply, then verify the link actually contains the claim and disclose AI help where required.
Let AI invent plausible-looking sources to fill the reference list.
Use AI to remove all citations so the slides look cleaner.
problems.explanation: AI can format references you provide, but you must verify the source and disclose AI use; fabricated citations are an integrity violation.

problems.stem: A reviewer says one citation is 'just a URL.' Which revision makes it verifiable?
options: Replace it with 'Author/Org, title, year, and a link to the exact page that states the 18% figure.'
Move the URL to the last slide.
problems.explanation: A verifiable citation names author, title, year, and points to the exact location of the claim, not a bare link.
